title: Asset-Liability Management (ALM) & Interest Rate Risk: Structural Liquidity Statements, Dynamic Duration Gap Modeling & Earning at Risk (EaR) Simulations
description: Master executive bank asset-liability management (ALM) and market risk governance. Formulate the institutional ALCO charter, model the regulatory Structural Liquidity Statement across statutory time buckets enforcing Basel III prudential net outflow tolerance ceilings, analyze Interest Rate Sensitivity Statements classifying balance sheet items into Rate Sensitive Assets (RSA) and Rate Sensitive Liabilities (RSL), compute dynamic Duration Gap (DGAP) and calculate the Economic Value of Equity (EVE) sensitivity to yield curve shifts, execute Earnings at Risk (EaR) simulations modeling Net Interest Income (NII) shocks, and establish dynamic contingency funding and interest rate derivative hedging strategies.
goal: Empower ALM desk heads, treasury market risk officers, and ALCO members to measure, stress test, and hedge balance-sheet structural liquidity mismatches and interest rate risks under Basel III IRRBB standards.
recap: In Day 38, we mastered sovereign debt trading, primary auctions, and quantitative duration-convexity metrics. Today in Day 39, we scale from single-instrument trading to total enterprise balance-sheet governance: Asset-Liability Management (ALM), ensuring bank solvency against structural liquidity runs and interest rate shocks.

parts.title: The Institutional ALCO Framework & Regulatory Structural Liquidity Statement
say: Asset-Liability Management (ALM) is the strategic, dynamic management of a commercial bank's entire balance sheet to optimize profitability while ensuring perpetual solvency and liquidity under both benign and stressed macroeconomic environments. Unlike industrial corporations where balance sheets primarily support production, in banking, the balance sheet IS the business. The inherent economic function of commercial banks is 'maturity transformation' and 'liquidity transformation'—accepting short-term, highly liquid customer deposits and transforming them into long-term, illiquid commercial loans and mortgages. This structural transformation generates substantial Net Interest Margin (NIM), but exposes the institution to two existential vulnerabilities: Structural Liquidity Risk (the risk of sudden cash runoffs outstripping available liquid funds) and Interest Rate Risk (the risk of margin compression and capital erosion caused by shifts in benchmark yield curves).

The Asset-Liability Committee (ALCO) Governance Charter: To maintain sovereign and regulatory solvency, modern banking standards mandate the establishment of an executive Asset-Liability Committee (ALCO). Chaired by the Chief Executive Officer or Managing Director and comprising the Chief Financial Officer (CFO), Chief Risk Officer (CRO), Head of Global Treasury, Head of Wholesale Banking, Head of Retail Banking, and Chief Economist, ALCO serves as the supreme balance sheet command authority. Meeting at least monthly (and convened within minutes during liquidity crises), ALCO is legally responsible for: (1) Formulating enterprise balance sheet growth targets and pricing strategies for deposits and advances; (2) Enforcing prudential limits on structural maturity mismatches and interest rate exposures; (3) Establishing internal transfer pricing (Funds Transfer Pricing - FTP) mechanisms to incentivize efficient capital allocation across branches; and (4) Formulating and testing the bank's Contingency Funding Plan (CFP) under simulated stress scenarios.

The Mechanics of the Structural Liquidity Statement: The primary diagnostic tool utilized by ALCO and central bank supervisory examiners to audit structural liquidity is the Structural Liquidity Statement (SLS). The SLS requires the bank to map all existing asset and liability cash flows into standardized chronological maturity buckets based on their contractual or behavioral cash-flow timing: (1) Next Day (Day 1); (2) 2 to 7 Days; (3) 8 to 14 Days; (4) 15 to 30 Days; (5) 31 Days to 2 Months; (6) 2 to 3 Months; (7) 3 to 6 Months; (8) 6 Months to 1 Year; (9) 1 to 3 Years; (10) 3 to 5 Years; and (11) Over 5 Years.

Inflows, Outflows, and Net Cumulative Mismatches: In each maturity bucket, the treasury desk calculates: Total Cash Inflows (repayment of loan installments, maturing interbank placements, coupon receipts, maturing T-Bills) minus Total Cash Outflows (maturing term deposits, anticipated savings account withdrawals, loan drawdowns, operating expenditures). This yields the Net Mismatch (Gap) for that specific bucket. Summing these net gaps sequentially across time generates the Cumulative Net Mismatch. If cumulative outflows exceed cumulative inflows, a structural liquidity deficit exists, requiring the bank to raise fresh wholesale funding or liquidate liquid assets to avoid default.

Basel III and Supervisory Prudential Tolerance Limits: Because short-term liquidity deficits can trigger systemic runs, central banks impose rigid prudential caps on cumulative negative mismatches in short-term buckets: (1) Next Day (Day 1): Cumulative negative mismatch cannot exceed 5% of cumulative cash outflows; (2) 2 to 7 Days: Negative mismatch capped at 10% of cumulative outflows; (3) 8 to 14 Days: Negative mismatch capped at 15% of cumulative outflows; and (4) 15 to 30 Days: Negative mismatch capped at 20% of cumulative outflows. Any breach of these statutory tolerance thresholds triggers mandatory supervisory reporting, immediate liquidity escalation, and emergency ALCO intervention.

Behavioral Modeling of Core Deposits and Uncommitted Lines: Contractual maturity does not equal behavioral reality. For instance, Current and Savings Account (CASA) deposits have zero contractual maturity (payable on demand), yet behaviorally, a significant portion—known as Core CASA—remains permanently embedded in the bank for years. ALCO uses statistical churn models, decaying run-off parameters, and historical volatility time-series to separate volatile CASA (allocated to short-term buckets) from stable core CASA (allocated to medium and long-term buckets). Similarly, uncommitted credit lines extended to corporate borrowers are modeled based on expected drawdown rates under stress.

By commanding the institutional ALCO charter, chronological maturity bucketing, behavioral cash-flow modeling, and statutory tolerance ceilings, treasury ALM directors safeguard institutional liquidity against catastrophic systemic freezes.
parts.example: Titan Bank audits its Next Day bucket: Expected cash inflows are $480M; expected cash outflows are $500M. The net negative mismatch is -$20M. With cumulative outflows at $500M, the negative mismatch represents -4.0% (-$20M / $500M), safely inside the regulatory -5.0% Basel tolerance ceiling.
parts.code:
def evaluate_structural_liquidity_statement(
    inflows: dict = None,
    outflows: dict = None,
    prudential_limits_pct: dict = None
) -> dict:
    # ALCO Structural Liquidity Statement (SLS) & Prudential Tolerance Engine
    if inflows is None:
        inflows = {
            'Day_1': 480.0,       # $ Millions
            'Days_2_to_7': 850.0,
            'Days_8_to_14': 620.0,
            'Days_15_to_30': 1100.0,
            'Days_31_to_90': 2400.0
        }
    if outflows is None:
        outflows = {
            'Day_1': 500.0,
            'Days_2_to_7': 900.0,
            'Days_8_to_14': 700.0,
            'Days_15_to_30': 1250.0,
            'Days_31_to_90': 2200.0
        }
    if prudential_limits_pct is None:
        prudential_limits_pct = {
            'Day_1': -5.0,        # Max negative mismatch as % of cumulative outflows
            'Days_2_to_7': -10.0,
            'Days_8_to_14': -15.0,
            'Days_15_to_30': -20.0,
            'Days_31_to_90': -25.0
        }
        
    bucket_analysis = []
    cum_inflows = 0.0
    cum_outflows = 0.0
    any_breach = False
    
    for bucket in inflows:
        inf = inflows[bucket]
        outf = outflows[bucket]
        net_gap = inf - outf
        
        cum_inflows += inf
        cum_outflows += outf
        cum_gap = cum_inflows - cum_outflows
        
        cum_gap_pct_of_outflows = (cum_gap / cum_outflows) * 100.0
        limit = prudential_limits_pct.get(bucket, -100.0)
        breached = cum_gap_pct_of_outflows < limit
        if breached:
            any_breach = True
            
        bucket_analysis.append({
            'bucket': bucket,
            'inflows_usd_m': inf,
            'outflows_usd_m': outf,
            'net_bucket_gap_usd_m': round(net_gap, 2),
            'cum_gap_usd_m': round(cum_gap, 2),
            'cum_gap_pct': round(cum_gap_pct_of_outflows, 2),
            'prudential_limit_pct': limit,
            'compliant': not breached
        })
        
    return {
        'total_audited_inflows_m': cum_inflows,
        'total_audited_outflows_m': cum_outflows,
        'final_cum_gap_m': round(cum_gap, 2),
        'regulatory_compliance_status': not any_breach,
        'bucket_dockets': bucket_analysis
    }

sls_res = evaluate_structural_liquidity_statement()
print("=== ALCO Regulatory Structural Liquidity Statement (SLS) Docket ===")
print(f"Total Inflows Audited:   ${sls_res['total_audited_inflows_m']:,.1f} Million")
print(f"Total Outflows Audited:  ${sls_res['total_audited_outflows_m']:,.1f} Million")
print(f"All Tolerance Ceilings Met: {sls_res['regulatory_compliance_status']}")
print("\n--- Structural Liquidity Time Bucket Analysis ---")
for b in sls_res['bucket_dockets']:
    status = "PASS" if b['compliant'] else "BREACH!"
    print(f"{b['bucket']:15} | Net: ${b['net_bucket_gap_usd_m']:>6.1f}M | Cum Gap: ${b['cum_gap_usd_m']:>6.1f}M ({b['cum_gap_pct']:>5.2f}% vs Limit {b['prudential_limit_pct']:>5.1f}%) | [{status}]")

check.question: What is the primary regulatory purpose of imposing a maximum negative cumulative mismatch limit (such as -5% in Day 1) in a bank's Structural Liquidity Statement?
options: To prevent banks from over-relying on volatile overnight wholesale borrowings to fund illiquid assets, ensuring structural liquidity survival during market freezes.
To force commercial banks to shut down all ATM branches.
To prohibit customers from depositing funds into savings accounts.
To replace cash currency with physical gold bullion.
check.why: Prudential mismatch limits prevent banks from excessive short-term maturity transformation, safeguarding them against catastrophic liquidity runs.

parts.title: Interest Rate Sensitivity Analysis: Rate Sensitive Assets (RSA), RSL & Repricing Gap
say: While structural liquidity statements govern cash-flow timing, commercial banks face equal risk from interest rate fluctuations. Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB) represents the risk to a bank's capital and earnings arising from adverse movements in interest rates that affect its banking book positions. When market benchmark rates fluctuate, the interest rates earned on assets and paid on liabilities reprice at different speeds, volumes, and frequencies. To evaluate this exposure, ALCO constructs the Interest Rate Sensitivity Statement (IRSS).

Taxonomy of Rate-Sensitive Items: Balance sheet assets and liabilities are classified into two critical operational categories: (1) Rate-Sensitive Assets (RSA): Assets that will experience an interest rate change (repricing) or maturity within a designated time window. RSAs include floating-rate corporate loans (pegged to Repo or SOFR), variable-rate mortgages, maturing commercial paper, Treasury Bills, and repo placements; (2) Rate-Sensitive Liabilities (RSL): Liabilities that will mature or reprice within the identical time horizon. RSLs include wholesale certificates of deposit, maturing fixed term deposits, floating-rate borrowings, and repo borrowings. Assets and liabilities that do not reprice within the window (such as fixed-rate 15-year loans, long-term perpetual subordinated debt, fixed assets, and equity capital) are classified as Non-Rate-Sensitive.

The Repricing Gap Equation: The fundamental measure of short-term interest rate risk is the Repricing Gap (GAP): GAP = Rate-Sensitive Assets (RSA) - Rate-Sensitive Liabilities (RSL). Alternatively, ALCO tracks the Sensitivity Gap Ratio: Gap Ratio = RSA / RSL. Depending on the sign of the Gap, a bank operates in one of three structural profiles: (1) Asset-Sensitive Balance Sheet (Positive Gap: RSA > RSL, Gap Ratio > 1.0): More assets reprice than liabilities over the specified horizon. If benchmark interest rates rise, asset yields reprice upward faster than funding costs, expanding Net Interest Income (NII). However, if interest rates fall, asset yields drop while funding costs lag, causing margin contraction; (2) Liability-Sensitive Balance Sheet (Negative Gap: RSA < RSL, Gap Ratio < 1.0): More liabilities reprice than assets. If interest rates fall, deposit and borrowing costs plunge faster than asset yields, driving dramatic NIM expansion. Conversely, if interest rates rise, funding costs surge while fixed asset yields remain trapped, leading to severe earnings compression; and (3) Perfectly Hedged / Neutral Balance Sheet (Zero Gap: RSA = RSL, Gap Ratio = 1.0): Asset and liability repricing perfectly offset each other, immunizing Net Interest Income from interest rate shifts.

Cumulative Gap Profiling Across Maturity Horizons: ALCO computes the Repricing Gap across identical time buckets as the liquidity statement (e.g., 1-28 Days, 29-90 Days, 91-180 Days, 181-365 Days). This multi-horizon analysis prevents maturity masking—where a bank appears neutral over a 1-year aggregate horizon but harbors a massive negative gap in the 30-day window and an offsetting positive gap in the 9-month window, creating intense interim vulnerability to rate spikes.

Basis Risk, Yield Curve Risk, and Option Risk: Standard Gap analysis assumes parallel shifts in rates across all products. In reality, IRRBB encompasses three complex sub-risks: (1) Basis Risk: The risk that rates on RSAs and RSLs shift by different magnitudes even if they reprice at the same time (e.g. lending yields pegged to 3-month Treasury yields while deposit costs are pegged to Central Bank policy rates); (2) Yield Curve Risk: The risk of non-parallel yield curve changes (steepening, flattening, or twists) that impact assets and liabilities situated at different tenors; and (3) Embedded Option Risk: The risk that customers exercise options embedded in bank contracts—such as borrowers prepaying fixed-rate mortgages when interest rates plummet, or depositors breaking fixed deposits early to reinvest at higher rates when interest rates spike.

By mastering RSA and RSL taxonomy, the mathematical physics of positive versus negative Repricing Gaps, and the multi-dimensional nuances of basis and option risks, bank treasury desks engineer optimal structural balance sheets that defend Net Interest Income across all phases of the macroeconomic cycle.
parts.example: Titan Bank has $12.0B in Rate-Sensitive Assets and $14.5B in Rate-Sensitive Liabilities over a 90-day horizon. The Repricing Gap is -$2.5B (Liability-Sensitive, Gap Ratio 0.828). If central bank rates rise by 100 bps (+1.00%), Titan's Net Interest Income drops by $25M per year (-$2.5B * 0.01).
parts.code:
def analyze_interest_rate_repricing_gap(
    rsa_usd_m: float = 12000.0,
    rsl_usd_m: float = 14500.0,
    rate_shift_bps_scenarios: list = None
) -> dict:
    # ALCO Repricing Gap & Net Interest Income (NII) Sensitivity Engine
    if rate_shift_bps_scenarios is None:
        rate_shift_bps_scenarios = [-100.0, -50.0, +25.0, +50.0, +100.0, +200.0]
        
    repricing_gap_m = rsa_usd_m - rsl_usd_m
    gap_ratio = rsa_usd_m / rsl_usd_m
    
    if repricing_gap_m > 0:
        profile = "ASSET_SENSITIVE (Benefits from Rate Hikes, Loses on Rate Cuts)"
    elif repricing_gap_m < 0:
        profile = "LIABILITY_SENSITIVE (Benefits from Rate Cuts, Loses on Rate Hikes)"
    else:
        profile = "NEUTRAL / IMMUNIZED"
        
    scenario_results = []
    for shift_bps in rate_shift_bps_scenarios:
        delta_y = shift_bps / 10000.0
        # Delta NII = GAP * Delta Yield
        delta_nii_m = repricing_gap_m * delta_y
        scenario_results.append({
            'rate_shift_bps': shift_bps,
            'delta_nii_usd_m': round(delta_nii_m, 2),
            'impact': 'EXPANSION' if delta_nii_m > 0 else ('COMPRESSION' if delta_nii_m < 0 else 'NEUTRAL')
        })
        
    return {
        'rsa_usd_m': rsa_usd_m,
        'rsl_usd_m': rsl_usd_m,
        'repricing_gap_usd_m': repricing_gap_m,
        'gap_ratio': round(gap_ratio, 3),
        'balance_sheet_profile': profile,
        'scenario_impacts': scenario_results
    }

gap_res = analyze_interest_rate_repricing_gap()
print("=== ALCO Interest Rate Sensitivity & Repricing Gap Docket ===")
print(f"Rate-Sensitive Assets (RSA):       ${gap_res['rsa_usd_m']:,.1f} Million")
print(f"Rate-Sensitive Liabilities (RSL):  ${gap_res['rsl_usd_m']:,.1f} Million")
print(f"Repricing Gap (RSA - RSL):        ${gap_res['repricing_gap_usd_m']:,.1f} Million")
print(f"Sensitivity Gap Ratio:             {gap_res['gap_ratio']}")
print(f"Balance Sheet Positioning:         {gap_res['balance_sheet_profile']}")
print("\n--- Projected Net Interest Income (NII) Shift Across Rate Scenarios ---")
for s in gap_res['scenario_impacts']:
    print(f"Rate Shift: {s['rate_shift_bps']:+6.0f} bps | Delta NII: ${s['delta_nii_usd_m']:+7.2f} Million | [{s['impact']}]")

parts.title: Dynamic Duration Gap Modeling & Economic Value of Equity (EVE) Physics
say: While Repricing Gap analysis measures the accounting impact on annual Net Interest Income, it suffers from a fatal blind spot: it ignores the long-term wealth destruction inflicted on the bank's underlying economic equity by changes in interest rates. When interest rates shift, the present market values of ALL future asset cash flows and liability obligations change simultaneously. To evaluate this fundamental long-term solvency risk, ALCO utilizes Duration Gap (DGAP) analysis and measures changes in the Economic Value of Equity (EVE).

Economic Value of Equity (EVE) Defined: The Economic Value of Equity (EVE) represents the economic net worth of the bank: the present value of all expected asset cash flows minus the present value of all expected liability cash flows: EVE = PV(Assets) - PV(Liabilities). Under Basel III Pillar 2 standards, central banks assess the resilience of a bank's capital through the EVE Sensitivity Test, requiring banks to subject their balance sheet to standardized +200 basis point and -200 basis point interest rate shocks.

The Duration Gap (DGAP) Formulation: The sensitivity of EVE to interest rate shifts is governed by the weighted-average duration of assets relative to liabilities, scaled by the bank's leverage ratio: DGAP = D_A - [ (Total Liabilities / Total Assets) * D_L ], where D_A is the weighted-average Macaulay or Modified Duration of total bank assets, and D_L is the weighted-average duration of total liabilities. Because commercial bank assets typically consist of long-term mortgages and term loans (long duration, e.g. D_A = 4.2 years) while liabilities consist of short-term customer deposits (short duration, e.g. D_L = 1.4 years), commercial banks almost universally maintain a Positive Duration Gap (DGAP > 0).

The Physics of EVE Sensitivity: The percentage change in the Economic Value of Equity for a given shift in benchmark yield (Delta y) is mathematically formulated as: Delta EVE = - [ D_A - (Liabilities / Assets) * D_L ] * Assets * [ Delta y / (1 + y) ] = - DGAP * Total Assets * [ Delta y / (1 + y) ]. This equation exposes the structural vulnerability of commercial banking: When DGAP is positive, a rise in interest rates (Delta y > 0) causes the market value of assets to collapse by far more than the market value of liabilities drops, wiping out massive amounts of bank economic equity! Conversely, if interest rates fall, the positive duration gap drives exponential increases in economic equity value.

Key Rate Duration (KRD) and Term Structure Decompositions: Because interest rate shifts are rarely parallel, advanced ALM desks decompose portfolio duration into Key Rate Durations (KRDs) across benchmark tenors (3-month, 1-year, 2-year, 5-year, 10-year, and 30-year). KRD isolates the sensitivity of EVE to a shift in a single specific maturity point while holding all other points constant. This enables treasury quants to detect curve steepening or inversion vulnerabilities that aggregate duration gap figures conceal.

The Basel III 15% / 20% Outlier Threshold: Under the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) IRRBB Framework, a commercial bank is designated as an 'Outlier Bank' if a standardized 200 basis point rate shock causes a decline in EVE exceeding 15% of its Tier 1 Capital (or 20% of Total Capital under older Basel guidelines). If a bank breaches the outlier threshold, supervisory authorities impose mandatory supervisory capital surcharges (Pillar 2 add-ons), restrict dividend payouts, and force the bank to immediately rebalance its duration gap using interest rate derivatives.

Immunization and Duration Matching: To immunize the bank's economic capital against interest rate risk, the treasury desk must drive DGAP toward zero: DGAP = 0 occurs when D_A = (Liabilities / Assets) * D_L. Because shrinking loan maturities damages customer relationships and lengthening retail deposit maturities is costly, ALCO achieves duration immunization synthetically in the wholesale derivatives market: entering into Receive-Fixed / Pay-Floating or Pay-Fixed Interest Rate Swaps (IRS) to dynamically calibrate balance sheet duration.

By commanding Duration Gap modeling, Key Rate Duration decomposition, EVE sensitivity physics, and Basel outlier capital constraints, treasury risk executives protect the bank's core economic net worth against catastrophic yield curve shocks.
parts.example: Titan Bank has $50B in Assets (D_A = 4.5 yrs), $45B in Liabilities (D_L = 1.5 yrs), and $5B in Equity. DGAP = 4.5 - (45/50 * 1.5) = 4.5 - 1.35 = +3.15 years. Under a +200 bps (+2.0%) rate shock (at y=7%), EVE drops by: -3.15 * $50B * (0.02 / 1.07) = -$2.94B, eroding 58.8% of bank equity ($2.94B / $5.0B) and severely breaching the Basel 15% Tier-1 outlier limit!
parts.code:
def evaluate_duration_gap_and_eve_sensitivity(
    total_assets_usd_b: float = 50.0,
    total_liabilities_usd_b: float = 45.0,
    duration_assets_years: float = 4.50,
    duration_liabilities_years: float = 1.50,
    current_interest_rate: float = 0.070,
    shock_bps: float = 200.0,
    tier1_capital_usd_b: float = 5.0
) -> dict:
    # ALCO Duration Gap & Economic Value of Equity (EVE) Engine
    economic_equity_usd_b = total_assets_usd_b - total_liabilities_usd_b
    leverage_ratio = total_liabilities_usd_b / total_assets_usd_b
    
    # Duration Gap (DGAP) = D_A - (L / A) * D_L
    duration_gap = duration_assets_years - (leverage_ratio * duration_liabilities_years)
    
    # Delta EVE = - DGAP * Assets * (Delta y / (1 + y))
    delta_y = shock_bps / 10000.0
    delta_eve_usd_b = - duration_gap * total_assets_usd_b * (delta_y / (1.0 + current_interest_rate))
    
    eve_drop_pct_of_capital = (abs(delta_eve_usd_b) / tier1_capital_usd_b) * 100.0
    is_basel_outlier = eve_drop_pct_of_capital > 15.0 # Basel III IRRBB 15% Tier 1 Limit
    
    # Immunized Duration of Liabilities required to make DGAP = 0
    immunized_d_l = duration_assets_years / leverage_ratio
    
    return {
        'total_assets_b': total_assets_usd_b,
        'total_liabilities_b': total_liabilities_usd_b,
        'economic_equity_b': round(economic_equity_usd_b, 2),
        'duration_assets_years': duration_assets_years,
        'duration_liabilities_years': duration_liabilities_years,
        'duration_gap_years': round(duration_gap, 3),
        'rate_shock_bps': shock_bps,
        'delta_eve_usd_b': round(delta_eve_usd_b, 3),
        'capital_depletion_pct': round(eve_drop_pct_of_capital, 2),
        'basel_outlier_breached': is_basel_outlier,
        'immunized_liabilities_duration_target': round(immunized_d_l, 2)
    }

eve_res = evaluate_duration_gap_and_eve_sensitivity()
print("=== ALCO Duration Gap (DGAP) & EVE Sensitivity Docket ===")
print(f"Total Balance Sheet Assets:     ${eve_res['total_assets_b']:.1f} Billion (Duration: {eve_res['duration_assets_years']} yrs)")
print(f"Total Balance Sheet Liabilities:  ${eve_res['total_liabilities_b']:.1f} Billion (Duration: {eve_res['duration_liabilities_years']} yrs)")
print(f"Bank Economic Equity (EVE):     ${eve_res['economic_equity_b']:.1f} Billion")
print(f"Duration Gap (DGAP):            +{eve_res['duration_gap_years']} years (Positive Gap)")
print("\n--- Basel III Standardized +200 bps Interest Rate Shock Test ---")
print(f"Modeled Economic Value Shift:   ${eve_res['delta_eve_usd_b']:.3f} Billion ({eve_res['delta_eve_usd_b']*1e3:,.1f} Million)")
print(f"Tier 1 Capital Depletion:       {eve_res['capital_depletion_pct']:.2f}% (Statutory Limit: 15.0%)")
print(f"Basel III Outlier Bank Status:  BREACHED: {eve_res['basel_outlier_breached']} (Supervisory Capital Surcharge Imposed!)")
print(f"Immunization Target D_L:        {eve_res['immunized_liabilities_duration_target']} years required for DGAP = 0")

parts.title: Earnings at Risk (EaR) & Net Interest Margin (NIM) Stress Simulation
say: While EVE measures long-term economic net worth, executive bank management and equity shareholders evaluate quarter-to-quarter financial performance through Net Interest Income (NII) and Net Interest Margin (NIM): NIM = Net Interest Income / Average Earning Assets. To safeguard accounting earnings against rate volatility, treasury risk desks run sophisticated Earnings at Risk (EaR) simulations.

Earnings at Risk (EaR) Defined: Earnings at Risk (EaR) models the maximum potential loss in Net Interest Income over a specified operating horizon (typically 12 months) resulting from adverse movements in interest rates at a designated confidence level (such as 95% or 99%). EaR expands simple Repricing Gap calculations into dynamic multi-variable stochastic simulations, incorporating dynamic balance sheet growth assumptions, customer behavior, and non-parallel yield curve shocks.

The Impact of Embedded Options: In a static world, assets and liabilities reprice purely according to their contractual schedules. In the real world, customers actively exercise embedded financial options when rates change: (1) Prepayment Risk (Call Option on Assets): When mortgage rates drop by 150 bps, prime retail borrowers refinance their 7.5% mortgages at 6.0%. This accelerates prepayments precisely when the bank has to reinvest that cash into low-yielding assets; and (2) Early Withdrawal Risk (Put Option on Liabilities): When term deposit rates rise from 5.0% to 7.5%, depositors pay nominal early withdrawal penalty fees to break existing 5.0% term deposits and roll into new 7.5% deposits, forcing funding costs to surge much faster than contractual schedules predict.

Non-Parallel Yield Curve Scenarios in EaR Modeling: Treasury quant desks model four distinct non-parallel term structure shocks: (1) Bear Steepener: Long-term yields rise faster than short-term yields, widening lending margins for asset-sensitive banks; (2) Bear Flattener: Short-term policy rates jump while long-term rates remain sluggish, rapidly driving up funding costs for liability-sensitive banks; (3) Bull Steepener: Central bank aggressively slashes policy rates while long-term rates remain stable, drastically reducing borrowing costs; and (4) Bull Flattener: Long-term yields plunge faster than short-term rates, compressing asset yields without providing equivalent liability relief.

Core Deposit Behavioral Decay and FTP Framework: The most critical assumption in EaR simulation is the behavior of non-maturity deposits (CASA). If ALCO assumes all CASA deposits are 100% sticky and pay 0% or 3% perpetually, the model severely understates funding risk. Under rising rate environments, corporate clients sweep idle balances into high-yielding money market funds or wholesale CDs (a phenomenon known as 'deposit beta'). Treasury implements Funds Transfer Pricing (FTP) systems to charge business lines for the liquidity and interest rate options their products consume, ensuring that retail branch managers price deposits and loans with full awareness of embedded IRRBB costs.

Stochastic Rate Path Generation and Monte Carlo Simulation: Leading institutions execute Monte Carlo term structure simulations generating tens of thousands of correlated interest rate paths utilizing the Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (CIR) or Hull-White two-factor short-rate models. These stochastic engines simulate simultaneous shifts across interest rate levels, slopes, and curvatures, providing a probability density function of future Net Interest Income. By analyzing the 95th and 99th percentile lower tails, ALCO establishes hard earnings-at-risk capital reserves to ensure uninterrupted profitability across turbulent economic cycles.

Dynamic Balance Sheet Reinvestment and Credit Spread Elasticity: Beyond static repricing schedules, enterprise EaR models simulate dynamic management actions and balance sheet reinvestment strategies over multi-year horizons. As high-yielding corporate loans mature during credit expansions, the model simulates loan run-off replacement at competitive market spreads while incorporating credit spread widening during recessionary phases. This dynamic synthesis of volume growth, spread elasticity, and interest rate volatility empowers ALCO to design proactive product pricing architectures that protect shareholder dividends against margin compression.

By mastering dynamic EaR simulation, customer embedded option modeling, deposit beta analytics, stochastic Monte Carlo pathing, and non-parallel yield curve stress testing, bank treasury directors protect annual Net Interest Margin from unexpected macroeconomic shocks.
parts.example: Titan Bank models a Bear Flattener scenario (+150 bps short rates, +50 bps long rates) on a $30B balance sheet. With an empirical deposit beta of 0.65 on $18B in CASA, funding costs rise by $175.5M while earning assets generate only $120.0M, resulting in a Net Interest Income contraction of -$55.5M (EaR of 18.5% of annual NII).
parts.code:
def simulate_earnings_at_risk_and_nim(
    earning_assets_usd_m: float = 30000.0,
    weighted_asset_yield: float = 0.075,
    total_liabilities_usd_m: float = 27000.0,
    weighted_funding_cost: float = 0.045,
    short_rate_shock_bps: float = 150.0,
    long_rate_shock_bps: float = 50.0,
    deposit_beta: float = 0.65,
    rsa_share: float = 0.40,
    rsl_share: float = 0.60
) -> dict:
    # Dynamic Earnings at Risk (EaR) & Net Interest Margin (NIM) Simulation Engine
    base_nii_usd_m = (earning_assets_usd_m * weighted_asset_yield) - (total_liabilities_usd_m * weighted_funding_cost)
    base_nim_pct = (base_nii_usd_m / earning_assets_usd_m) * 100.0
    
    # Bear Flattener Shock Dynamics:
    # RSAs reprice at blended rate (partially short, partially long): e.g. 50% short, 50% long = +100 bps
    blended_asset_shock_bps = (0.5 * short_rate_shock_bps) + (0.5 * long_rate_shock_bps)
    # RSLs reprice heavily against short rates modulated by deposit beta: short_rate_shock * deposit_beta
    effective_liability_shock_bps = short_rate_shock_bps * deposit_beta
    
    # Repricing Volumes
    repricing_assets_m = earning_assets_usd_m * rsa_share
    repricing_liabilities_m = total_liabilities_usd_m * rsl_share
    
    # Incremental Interest Inflows and Outflows
    incremental_interest_income = repricing_assets_m * (blended_asset_shock_bps / 10000.0)
    incremental_interest_expense = repricing_liabilities_m * (effective_liability_shock_bps / 10000.0)
    
    shocked_nii_m = base_nii_usd_m + incremental_interest_income - incremental_interest_expense
    delta_nii_m = shocked_nii_m - base_nii_usd_m
    ear_loss_m = max(0.0, -delta_nii_m)
    ear_pct_of_base_nii = (ear_loss_m / base_nii_usd_m) * 100.0
    
    shocked_nim_pct = (shocked_nii_m / earning_assets_usd_m) * 100.0
    delta_nim_bps = (shocked_nim_pct - base_nim_pct) * 100.0
    
    return {
        'base_nii_usd_m': round(base_nii_usd_m, 2),
        'base_nim_pct': round(base_nim_pct, 3),
        'incremental_asset_income_m': round(incremental_interest_income, 2),
        'incremental_liability_expense_m': round(incremental_interest_expense, 2),
        'shocked_nii_usd_m': round(shocked_nii_m, 2),
        'delta_nii_usd_m': round(delta_nii_m, 2),
        'earnings_at_risk_m': round(ear_loss_m, 2),
        'ear_pct_of_nii': round(ear_pct_of_base_nii, 2),
        'shocked_nim_pct': round(shocked_nim_pct, 3),
        'delta_nim_bps': round(delta_nim_bps, 1)
    }

ear_sim = simulate_earnings_at_risk_and_nim()
print("=== ALCO Dynamic Earnings at Risk (EaR) & NIM Stress Docket ===")
print(f"Baseline Net Interest Income (NII):   ${ear_sim['base_nii_usd_m']:,.2f} Million")
print(f"Baseline Net Interest Margin (NIM):   {ear_sim['base_nim_pct']:.3f}%")
print("\n--- Bear Flattener Macroeconomic Rate Shock Simulation ---")
print(f"Incremental Asset Interest Inflow:   +${ear_sim['incremental_asset_income_m']:,.2f} Million")
print(f"Incremental Funding Cost Surge:      -${ear_sim['incremental_liability_expense_m']:,.2f} Million (Deposit Beta: 0.65)")
print(f"Shocked Net Interest Income (NII):    ${ear_sim['shocked_nii_usd_m']:,.2f} Million")
print(f"Net Interest Margin Compression:     {ear_sim['delta_nim_bps']:.1f} bps (NIM dropped to {ear_sim['shocked_nim_pct']:.3f}%)")
print(f"Earnings at Risk (EaR Loss):          ${ear_sim['earnings_at_risk_m']:,.2f} Million ({ear_sim['ear_pct_of_nii']:.2f}% of NII)")

parts.title: Comprehensive Enterprise ALM Command & Balance Sheet Crisis Simulator
say: In this capstone operational phase of Day 39, we synthesize the structural liquidity statement, repricing gaps, dynamic duration gaps, EVE physics, and EaR simulations into a high-stakes enterprise ALM command simulator. You assume the role of Chief Risk Officer and ALCO Executive Director of Titan National Bank, an enterprise institution commanding a $50,000,000,000 balance sheet ($45B in liabilities, $5B in Tier-1 equity) facing an acute macroeconomic liquidity contraction and unexpected monetary policy shock.

The Simulated Macroeconomic Crisis: At 9:00 AM on Monday, the Central Bank issues a surprise announcement: to halt surging inflation and stabilize the sovereign currency, the benchmark policy rate is hiked by 150 basis points (+1.50%). Simultaneously, interbank wholesale liquidity dries up, triggering an institutional deposit run-off of $1,200,000,000 across the 1-to-7 day window.

Diagnostic Audit 1 - Structural Liquidity Deficit: The simulator audits Titan's short-term liquidity position. In the Days 2-to-7 bucket, cash inflows total $850,000,000 against suddenly spiked cash outflows of $1,600,000,000 (reflecting the $1.2B run-off). The net negative mismatch in the bucket explodes to -$750,000,000, driving the cumulative negative mismatch to -$820,000,000 across $2,100,000,000 in cumulative outflows (-39.05%). This massive negative gap completely blows past the statutory Basel tolerance limit of -10.0%, triggering an immediate Level-1 Liquidity Emergency!

Diagnostic Audit 2 - EVE Capital Destruction & Basel Outlier Breach: Simultaneously, the market risk desk assesses the interest rate shock. Titan's balance sheet carries a weighted asset duration of 4.60 years ($50B) against a liability duration of 1.40 years ($45B). The resulting Duration Gap (DGAP) is: DGAP = 4.60 - (45/50 * 1.40) = +3.34 years. Under the +150 bps rate shock (at y=7.0%), the loss in Economic Value of Equity calculates to: Delta EVE = - 3.34 * $50B * (0.015 / 1.07) = -$2,341,121,495! This catastrophic $2.34B drop erodes 46.82% of Titan Bank's $5.0B Tier-1 capital, severely breaching the Basel III 15% outlier ceiling and placing the bank at risk of regulatory intervention.

Executing the Integrated ALCO Crisis Resolution Action Plan: Convening an emergency ALCO meeting at 10:30 AM, you execute a four-part balance sheet stabilization maneuver: (1) Activating the Contingency Funding Plan (CFP): Titan immediately pledges $1,500,000,000 of unencumbered G-Secs from its SLR investment book into the central bank's Standing Liquidity Facility (SLF) and TREPS market, injecting $1,470,000,000 of cash into the Days 2-to-7 bucket. This reduces the cumulative negative gap to -$50,000,000 (-2.38%), fully restoring statutory compliance within Basel tolerance limits; (2) Synthetic Balance Sheet Duration Immunization: To neutralize the positive DGAP without dumping long-term customer loans, the treasury desk enters into a $15,000,000,000 notional 5-year Pay-Fixed / Receive-Floating Interest Rate Swap (IRS) with a duration of -4.2 years. The swap injects negative duration, slashing Titan's effective Duration Gap from +3.34 years down to +0.82 years; (3) Capital Preservation: Post-swap, the revised EVE drop under the +150 bps shock shrinks from -$2.34B down to -$574,766,355 (11.5% of Tier-1 capital), bringing the bank safely beneath the 15% Basel outlier limit; and (4) FTP Dynamic Margin Recalibration: ALCO adjusts internal Funds Transfer Pricing by +125 bps, forcing retail branches to pass through funding costs to corporate borrowers, insulating annual Net Interest Margin.

Regulatory Capital Adequacy and CAMELS Supervisory Examination: The Board Risk Management Committee and central bank examiners audit the executed crisis protocol. Under the supervisory CAMELS rating framework, the bank's rapid defense of Liquidity (L) and Sensitivity to Market Risk (S) prevents supervisory downgrades and mandatory capital conservation buffers. By maintaining Tier-1 capital above 13.5% and restoring positive structural liquidity across all 8 statutory buckets, Titan National Bank establishes institutional gold-standard ALM resilience.

Regulatory Reporting and Supervisory Restoration: By 4:00 PM, the updated Structural Liquidity Statement and EVE sensitivity filings are submitted to the central bank's banking supervision department. The emergency actions preserve 100% of depositor safety, eliminate regulatory fines, and prove the institutional resilience of the bank's ALM framework.

By commanding this integrated enterprise ALM war room simulation, risk directors demonstrate complete executive readiness to measure, stress test, and immunize bank balance sheets against structural liquidity runs and extreme interest rate shocks.
parts.example: Titan Bank faced a simultaneous $1.2B liquidity runoff (39% cumulative gap breach) and a +150 bps rate shock destroying $2.34B in EVE (46.8% capital hit). ALCO activated repo liquidity ($1.47B raised, gap restored to -2.38%) and executed a $15B pay-fixed swap (cutting DGAP to 0.82 yrs, EVE hit slashed to 11.5%), fully restoring solvency.
parts.code:
def run_titan_enterprise_alm_crisis_simulator(
    total_assets_b: float = 50.0,
    total_liabilities_b: float = 45.0,
    tier1_capital_b: float = 5.0,
    d_assets_years: float = 4.60,
    d_liabilities_years: float = 1.40,
    rate_shock_bps: float = 150.0,
    repo_liquidity_activated_b: float = 1.470,
    irs_swap_notional_b: float = 15.0,
    irs_swap_duration: float = -4.20
) -> dict:
    # Phase 5 Comprehensive Enterprise ALM Command & Crisis Simulation Engine
    leverage_ratio = total_liabilities_b / total_assets_b
    
    # 1. Pre-Crisis Duration Gap & EVE Shock Audit
    initial_dgap = d_assets_years - (leverage_ratio * d_liabilities_years)
    delta_y = rate_shock_bps / 10000.0
    initial_delta_eve_b = - initial_dgap * total_assets_b * (delta_y / 1.07)
    initial_capital_erosion_pct = (abs(initial_delta_eve_b) / tier1_capital_b) * 100.0
    initial_basel_outlier = initial_capital_erosion_pct > 15.0
    
    # 2. Structural Liquidity Runoff & CFP Intervention
    # Pre-intervention: Days 2-7 cumulative gap is -$820M on $2,100M outflows = -39.05%
    pre_intervention_cum_gap_m = -820.0
    cum_outflows_m = 2100.0
    pre_intervention_gap_pct = (pre_intervention_cum_gap_m / cum_outflows_m) * 100.0
    pre_sls_breach = pre_intervention_gap_pct < -10.0
    
    # Post-intervention with Repo Cash Injection
    post_intervention_cum_gap_m = pre_intervention_cum_gap_m + (repo_liquidity_activated_b * 1000.0)
    post_intervention_gap_pct = (post_intervention_cum_gap_m / cum_outflows_m) * 100.0
    post_sls_compliant = post_intervention_gap_pct >= -10.0
    
    # 3. IRS Derivative Duration Immunization Mechanics
    # Swap contribution to asset duration: (Swap Notional / Total Assets) * Swap Duration
    swap_duration_impact = (irs_swap_notional_b / total_assets_b) * irs_swap_duration
    post_hedge_d_assets = d_assets_years + swap_duration_impact
    post_hedge_dgap = post_hedge_d_assets - (leverage_ratio * d_liabilities_years)
    
    post_hedge_delta_eve_b = - post_hedge_dgap * total_assets_b * (delta_y / 1.07)
    post_hedge_capital_erosion_pct = (abs(post_hedge_delta_eve_b) / tier1_capital_b) * 100.0
    post_hedge_basel_compliant = post_hedge_capital_erosion_pct <= 15.0
    
    return {
        'initial_dgap_years': round(initial_dgap, 3),
        'initial_eve_loss_m': round(initial_delta_eve_b * 1000.0, 2),
        'initial_capital_erosion_pct': round(initial_capital_erosion_pct, 2),
        'initial_basel_outlier_breached': initial_basel_outlier,
        'pre_liquidity_gap_pct': round(pre_intervention_gap_pct, 2),
        'pre_sls_breached': pre_sls_breach,
        'post_liquidity_gap_pct': round(post_intervention_gap_pct, 2),
        'post_sls_compliant': post_sls_compliant,
        'post_hedge_dgap_years': round(post_hedge_dgap, 3),
        'post_hedge_eve_loss_m': round(post_hedge_delta_eve_b * 1000.0, 2),
        'post_hedge_capital_erosion_pct': round(post_hedge_capital_erosion_pct, 2),
        'post_hedge_basel_compliant': post_hedge_basel_compliant
    }

alm_sim = run_titan_enterprise_alm_crisis_simulator()
print("=== Titan National Bank - Enterprise ALM Crisis Command Simulator ===")
print(f"Pre-Crisis Duration Gap:              +{alm_sim['initial_dgap_years']} years")
print(f"Unhedged EVE Economic Loss:           -${abs(alm_sim['initial_eve_loss_m']):,.2f} Million")
print(f"Initial Tier-1 Capital Depletion:     {alm_sim['initial_capital_erosion_pct']:.2f}% (Basel Outlier: {alm_sim['initial_basel_outlier_breached']})")
print(f"Pre-CFP Structural Liquidity Gap:     {alm_sim['pre_liquidity_gap_pct']:.2f}% (Tolerance Breach: {alm_sim['pre_sls_breached']})")
print("\n--- ALCO Emergency Crisis Resolution Execution ---")
print(f"1. Repo Cash Liquidity Injected:      +$1,470.0 Million (Pledged unencumbered G-Secs)")
print(f"   Post-CFP Structural Liquidity Gap: {alm_sim['post_liquidity_gap_pct']:.2f}% (Statutory Compliance Restored: {alm_sim['post_sls_compliant']})")
print(f"2. Synthetic IRS Swap Executed:       $15.0 Billion Notional Pay-Fixed Swaps (Duration: -4.20 yrs)")
print(f"   Post-Hedge Duration Gap:           +{alm_sim['post_hedge_dgap_years']} years (Reduced from +{alm_sim['initial_dgap_years']} yrs!)")
print(f"   Post-Hedge EVE Economic Loss:      -${abs(alm_sim['post_hedge_eve_loss_m']):,.2f} Million (Loss Reduced by 75.5%!)")
print(f"   Post-Hedge Tier-1 Capital Depletion:{alm_sim['post_hedge_capital_erosion_pct']:.2f}% (Safely Under 15.0% Limit: {alm_sim['post_hedge_basel_compliant']})")
print("Conclusion: Bank Solvency, Regulatory Capital & Liquidity Fully Defended!")
